meta.method: Independent final check of cards changed after the partw round. Each listed card's prior finding read; every cited page fetched afresh under an atlasforatlas.com User-Agent into the session scratchpad; all citation quotes machine-matched to the page text, with misses read by hand; the statement's changed claims, givers and footnotes read in context, with Wikipedia footnotes resolved from the rendered HTML and changed pins compared with Wikidata. Not a re-audit of the rest of each page.

na-e-002.note: Promise now credited to Xicotenga in Schmal (byline confirmed); Wikipedia's passage on Maxixcatzin and Xicotencatl the Elder is friendship and loyalty, as the card now says. 18th and 23rd both found.

na-e-018.note: Wikipedia's eleven and about 800 (500 men plus 300 women and children) credited; NPS's fourteen and about 1,500 found. December 1598, 22 January, prisoners and amputations hold.

na-e-020.note: Lamadrid's 70 now separate from the 400, which the card gives to the Pueblo Revolt article, where it stands. Lamadrid sentence found; stray space gone from the quote.

na-e-022.note: 1,500 and 28 now given to Wikipedia. Footnote on the 150 and 400 passage is Garrard, as stated. Bent, Montoya, Romero and the church hold.

na-e-024.note: Reordered correctly: $15 million package for the first draft, then the Senate's cut to 29,640 sq mi and $10 million; all on the page. Tohono O'odham claims found, attributed.

na-e-030.note: Force sizes and 'all but eight' now attributed to Wikipedia. Quotes and sequence (10 April, 28 and 30 April, 27 sold, 19 minutes) hold.

na-e-038.note: Pin fix holds: Wikidata Q128927906 carries a coordinate qualified as the mouth, 41.9424654, -103.9605034, as on the card. Approximate set. Treaty facts found.

na-e-039.note: 4,000 and 29 to 31 now attributed to the article (lead 29, infobox 31 per notes). Mormon's cow, High Forehead and 19 August found.

na-e-061.note: 'by Abe Farwell's account' is fair: the page has Farwell seeing Hammond fire, then the others' volleys. Graham's 13 and OTC's 20 and 300 found.

na-e-066.note: Both figures are on the page: 392 in the text, 350 in the infobox. Middleton's orders, 'punish Poundmaker', and DCB's 26 May, Regina trial and three years found.

na-e-078.note: Koehler's 5,000 is now the overall toll and Taylor's several hundred the winter deaths, as the page has it. Quote ends at 'individuals'. Copy slip only: 'at Newtown, razed' lacks 'and'.
na-e-078.fix: Copy: 'at Newtown, razed 40 villages' to 'at Newtown, and razed 40 villages'.

na-e-095.note: Page has 'The historian Betty Wood writes' with the 347 (footnote Wood 1997 p. 72); 'a quarter' is the same article's lead. 'About four hundred ... a third' found. Rest holds.

na-e-104.note: 'in Wikipedia's account' added to the 70; sentence found. NPS, Drake (footnote on that sentence) and the participant's figure found.

na-e-105.note: 90 men now attributed. Page has the party attacking two Niantic villages and burning them, then the Pequot village. Both Oldham accounts found.

na-e-108.note: 'by local tradition' gone; Uncas has Tracy and Leffingwell, stated as the card now credits it. Wawequa, June 1644, Confederation troops and the thirty-year peace found.

na-e-113.note: Two dozen now Grenier's: footnote grenier08, The Far Reaches of Empire, p. 84, on that sentence. Unattributed 200 and 80 are off the card; 'accounts of the dead vary' matches the page.

na-e-123.note: Participants now wendat and petun; Neutral gone. McMillan and Yellowhorn confirmed as the footnote on both figures, p. 78. Petun are the 'neighbours' in the title.

na-e-124.note: 'many fled ... where most starved' replaces the unattributed 10,000; found on Huron people. Dates hold on both pages.

na-e-136.note: 'between the Boyer and Nodaway rivers' follows the treaty text at OK State, both river quotes found. Iowa claim gone.

na-e-137.note: Footnote on 756 and 42 is Funk p. 47; on the 28 children, Funk pp. 45-46 and Madison p. 122. 'Arville Funk's count' holds.

na-e-140.note: Overreach gone; page's 'Spanish accounts at the time' sentence quoted and matches. Elvas's 2,500 and footnote 68 (Horwitz 2009) confirmed.

na-e-143.note: 'NCpedia has Moore losing 47 killed' matches the page's own voice. Footnote on the 33 and 1,000 is Shamlin. Graffenried's figures found.

na-e-145.note: Footnote on the tally is Barnett 2007 p. 105, with Boler 2006, so Barnett is a fair giver, but 'by a tally made a year later, by James Barnett' reads as if a 2007 author made the 1730 tally; the page says only that it 'was put at' those numbers, and the prior fix's 'reported' was dropped. Other facts found. Fix applied as proposed, 2026-10-31.
na-e-145.fix: Replace 'by a tally made a year later, by James Barnett' with 'by a tally made a year later, reported by James Barnett'.

na-e-147.note: Fort Prince George now named. 16 off the card. Footnote closing the two-dozen passage is Carroll Van West's Tennessee Encyclopedia entry. Grant's 1761 destruction found.

na-e-156.note: Vague giver gone; page has 'were reported to have survived'. Dates, route and the treaty hold.

na-e-164.note: Unattributed garrison numbers off the card. 'many' follows Wikipedia, with Smithsonian's 'nearly all' in notes. June 1802, mid-day, Unicorn and ransom found.

na-e-170.note: 100 off the card; 'may have killed many' stays within the page's hedge. Date 15 June, Lewis 'allegedly', clerk and Joseachal found.

na-e-175.note: 'though counts vary widely' gone. Glotov, hostage-taking and NLM's Solovief entry found, attributed.

na-e-186.note: 18 off the card; 'killed settlers' holds. NPS names Chapman, 'a volunteer', and gives 34 dead and 3 wounded.

na-e-187.note: Giver corrected: footnote on the 431 is Brown p. 410; bibliography has Brown, Mark H. (1967). NPS facts and Chapman as translator found. Housekeeping only: coord_source still names Q4870436 beside qid Q81351860.

na-e-192.note: Order fixed and antecedent given. Page has the militia's only fight with Palouse 'with no connection to the Whitman killings', ending by late March 1848, then five months more. Five names, trial and 3 June found.

na-e-194.note: Pin fix holds: Wikidata Q16890670 Council Grove State Park, 46.913, -114.155, as on the card. Page has the council at Council Grove and its monument there.

na-e-198.note: Giver named: the Coeur d'Alene War article has 'no decisive winner'. HistoryLink's fire, combined arms, 14 miles and one wounded found.

na-e-199.note: Giver named: Battle of Spokane Plains has 9-10 September, nearly 1,000, and 600 to 900. HistoryLink's 8 September and 800 found.

na-e-200.note: Giver named: Coeur d'Alene War has seventeen along Latah Creek. HistoryLink's account, including Owhi and the Bolon charge, found.

na-e-201.note: Giver named: Battle of Spokane Plains has 'document of surrender'. Headed text and date found on the treaty page; its Articles 2, 3 and 4 match the terms, so 'His terms' now stands on the primary text too. Tribe's chronology found.

na-e-203.note: Giver now named: USU page byline is Marley Madsen, 16 September 2020, and has the words used. Hedgpeth rightly not credited unread. Four tolls found. Copy slip only: stray ',.' after 'Bear River'.
na-e-203.fix: Copy: remove the comma in 'the Bear River,.'

na-e-207.note: Thatcher named; page has him citing Mooney for 1887. Eclipse vision and non-violence on the page, though no quote covers non-violence.

na-e-208.note: Givers named. Fariss and Smith 1882 is in the page's footnotes; block quote has Pit River and Weatherlow. Purdy's byline and Morehead 'and others' found.

na-e-209.note: NPS named for the 14; klamath off the participants (now modoc, usa). Woman, child, burned village, Jackson and Linkville militia found.

na-e-210.note: 163 credited to NPS, sentence found. Hanging, 2,000, Alcatraz and the two heads (Kintpuash) found.

na-e-216.note: Giver is what the page says: 'The National Park Service has estimated ... 60 of 400 ...; other accounts say 200'. Sherman's report and Ni'ka found.

na-e-217.note: 'authorised at two hundred men' follows the page's 'authorizing an organization of two hundred men'. 27 March, burning, Tenaya's son found.

na-e-218.note: Giver corrected: footnote on the 33 is 'Ishi: A Real-Life Last Of The Mohicans', Mohican Press. Burrill passage with Black Rock, the forty and the retaliation found.

na-e-219.note: Footnote on 70 to 90 is Greene, Nez Perce Summer, ch. 6. 'Gibbon losing 29, two more dying later' matches the page, and the summed 31 is gone. Gibbon's 17, 132 and 34 found on NPS.

na-e-220.note: Giver named: block quote is signed James H. Wilbur, Yakama Agent, 1881, and says the Secretary revoked his permission. No quote on the card carries the revocation, though the page does.
na-e-220.fix: Add a quote from Sarah Winnemucca: 'the Hon. Secretary revoked his permission'.
